pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 📝 **Strand 2 — Productivity Software**
Sub-strand 3: Introduction to Desktop Publishing

Flyers, posters, magazines, business cards and invitation cards are designed with desktop publishing software. In this unit you will learn the importance of DTP, create publications from blank pages and templates, and design your own flyer or card.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B8.2.3.1** Demonstrate how to use MS-Publisher.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B8.2.3.1.1** Explain the importance of desktop publishing software (DTP).
- **B8.2.3.1.2** Create and save a new document from a blank or pre-designed template.
- **B8.2.3.1.3** Demonstrate the use of the commands in MS-Publisher ribbons (Home, Page Design, Mailings, Review, View).
- **B8.2.3.1.4** Change the orientation and margins of a document.
- **B8.2.3.1.5** Add and modify pictures from different sources.
- **B8.2.3.1.6** Add and modify text.
- **B8.2.3.1.7∗** Create and present a Publisher document (flyer, advertisement, invitation cards, business cards).

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 6.1 The Importance of Desktop Publishing
- 6.2 Creating and Saving a Publication
- 6.3 Publisher Ribbon Commands
- 6.4 Changing Orientation and Margins
- 6.5 Adding and Modifying Pictures
- 6.6 Adding and Modifying Text
- 6.7 Creating and Presenting a Publication

**Core competencies developed:** Creativity and Innovation (CI5.4), Digital Literacy (DL5.1), Communication and Collaboration (CC9.6).

pages.title: The Importance of Desktop Publishing
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain the meaning of desktop publishing;
- state its importance;
- name DTP packages.
**Desktop publishing (DTP)** is the use of a computer and special software to design and produce publications that combine **text and graphics** in a precise, attractive **page layout**, such as newsletters, magazines, brochures, flyers, posters, certificates, calendars, business cards and invitation cards. Unlike a word processor, which flows text from page to page, DTP software places text and pictures in **frames (boxes)** that can be positioned anywhere on the page.
- Produces professional-quality designs quickly and cheaply, without a printing house.
- Precise control of layout, fonts, colours and pictures.
- Ready-made **templates** for many publication types.
- **Master pages** keep repeated items (logo, page numbers) the same on every page.
- Publications can be printed, saved as PDF, or published online; mail merge personalises cards and letters.
- Creates business opportunities: printing and design shops, branding services.
| **DTP software** | **Notes** |
|---|---|
| Microsoft Publisher | Easy, template-based; retired in October 2026 |
| Adobe InDesign | Industry standard for magazines, newspapers and books |
| QuarkXPress | Professional publishing software |
| Affinity Publisher | Professional DTP software, an alternative to InDesign |
| Scribus | Free and open-source |
| LibreOffice Draw | Free; good for flyers and posters |
| Canva, Microsoft Designer | Online design tools with many templates |

pages.title: Creating and Saving a Publication
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- open DTP software;
- create a document from a blank publication and from a template;
- save it with an appropriate name.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Creating from a blank page or a template (Publisher)**
1. Open **Publisher** from the Start menu.
2. For a blank page, click **Blank A4 (Portrait)** or **More Blank Page Sizes**.
3. For a template, click **Built-in** (or **Featured**) and choose a category, e.g. **Flyers**, **Business Cards** or **Invitation Cards**. Select a design, choose a **colour scheme** and **font scheme**, and click **Create**.
4. Click **File › Save As › Browse**, choose your folder, type a name such as B8_ScienceFair_Flyer and click **Save** (file type .pub). Use **File › Export › Create PDF/XPS** to save a PDF copy.

pages.title: Publisher Ribbon Commands
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explore the Home, Insert, Page Design, Mailings, Review and View ribbons.
| **Tab** | **Main commands** |
|---|---|
| Home | Clipboard, font and paragraph formatting, Styles, **Draw Text Box**, **Pictures**, Arrange (bring forward/back, group, align, wrap text), Find/Replace |
| Insert | Pages, Tables, Pictures (this device, online), Shapes, **Building Blocks** (page parts, calendars, borders, advertisements), Business Information, WordArt, Hyperlink, Header & Footer, Page Number |
| Page Design | Templates, **Margins**, **Orientation**, **Size**, Guides, **Master Pages**, **Colour schemes**, **Font schemes**, page **Background** |
| Mailings | **Mail Merge** to create personalised invitations, labels and certificates from a list of names; E-mail Merge |
| Review | Spelling, Research, Thesaurus, Language, Translate |
| View | Single Page / Two-Page Spread, Master Page, Boundaries, Guides, Rulers, Page Navigation, Zoom, Graphics Manager |
> 🧪 **Activity — Pair exploration**
Working in pairs, open a template and try at least two commands from each tab. Record what each command did in a table.

pages.title: Changing Orientation and Margins
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.4
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- change page orientation, size and margins.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Changing orientation and margins**
1. Click **Page Design › Orientation** and choose **Portrait** or **Landscape**.
2. Click **Page Design › Size** to choose A4, A5, business card, etc.
3. Click **Page Design › Margins** and choose **Narrow**, **Moderate** or **Wide**, or **Custom Margins** to enter exact values. The dashed **margin guides** show where text should stay.

pages.title: Adding and Modifying Pictures
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.5
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- insert pictures from different sources;
- modify pictures.
- **Insert › Pictures** (from your computer), **Online Pictures**, or drag a picture from File Explorer.
- Pictures can also come from a **scanner**, **digital camera**, phone (via USB/cloud) or a **screenshot**.
- Modify with the **Picture Format** tab: **Crop**, **Recolour**, **Corrections**, **Picture Styles**, **Picture Border**, **Rotate**, **Wrap Text** (square, tight, behind or in front of text), and **Change Picture** (swap the image but keep its size and position).

pages.title: Adding and Modifying Text
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.6
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- add text boxes;
- modify text with different fonts; link text boxes.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Working with text boxes**
1. Click **Home › Draw Text Box** and drag to draw a box.
2. Type or paste the text. Format it with the **Font** and **Paragraph** groups; use different **font types** for headings and body text.
3. Use the **Text Box Format** tab for columns, text direction, hyphenation and **text fit** options (e.g. Shrink Text on Overflow).
4. If text does not fit, an **overflow** indicator appears. Click it, then click inside another empty text box to **link** them so that the text flows on.

pages.title: Creating and Presenting a Publication
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.2.3.1.7
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- create a one-page publication: flyer, advertisement, invitation card or business card;
- present it to demonstrate creative ability.
| **Design principle** | **Meaning** |
|---|---|
| Balance | Distribute text and images evenly |
| Contrast | Make important items stand out (size, colour, boldness) |
| Alignment | Line up items with each other and the margins |
| White space | Leave empty space so the design is not crowded |
| Consistency | Use the same few fonts and colours throughout |
| Readability | Large, clear headings; no more than 2–3 fonts |
> 💻 **Practical session — Create and present**
Create **one** of the following: (a) a flyer for your school’s Science Fair; (b) an advertisement for a small business in your community; (c) an invitation card to your Speech and Prize-Giving Day; or (d) a business card for a local artisan. Include a picture, a headline, essential details (who, what, where, when), and contact information. Save as .pub and PDF, print or display it, and present your design decisions to the class.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Explain **four** ways DTP differs from word processing.
2. Describe the steps to create a business card from a template.
3. State **four** design principles for a good flyer.
4. Explain how to link text boxes when text overflows.
